steps.text:
Here's the plan. Steps that queue or start a print need your OK; the design steps don't.

1. Plan the two moving pieces (base and lid) with the hinge, then confirm the sizes on a sheet.
2. Build the base, the lid, and the hinge knuckles as separate bodies, with clearance at every joint.
3. Check the print-in-place gaps and the part against its plan.
4. Run the PETG job on the Prusa MK4S, slice it, and send it to the printer (needs your OK).

Starting with the plan.

args.part: SD card box with print-in-place hinge
assumptions: Standard SD card is 32 x 24 x 2.1 mm; the 56 x 36 x 18 mm interior holds several cards stacked or side by side.
Base is 20 mm tall and lid is 10 mm tall, so the closed box is 60 x 40 x 30 mm.
The lid skirt sits inside the base wall with 0.4 mm clearance per side (PETG on a 0.4 mm nozzle).
Hinge runs along the back 40 mm edge: base knuckles at both ends, lid knuckle in the middle, with a 2 mm pin bore.
The lid prints top down on the bed beside the base, 10 mm apart.
questions: Is a 2 mm pin bore fine, or do you want a separate printed or steel pin?
Do you want a finger notch on the lid edge?
